item.title: 90.4% of votes counted: No change in bloc distribution
item.description:
According to the partial official results of the elections for Israel's 26th Knesset, updated at 1:18 a.m., with approximately 90.4% of the votes counted, the distribution of seats remains unchanged. The current coalition holds 53 seats, the opposition bloc 48, and the Arab parties 19.
Likud leads with 26 seats, followed by Yashar with 21. The Joint List and Together each receive 12 seats, the Democrats eight, while Ra'am, Yisrael Beytenu, United Torah Judaism, Otzma Yehudit, and Shas each receive seven. The joint Religious Zionist-Zehut list receives six seats.
The Reservists-Economic Party remains below the electoral threshold with 2.63% of the vote, as does Amcha Yisrael with 1.6%.

item.title: Counting of double-envelope ballots begins in Israel's 26th Knesset elections
item.description:
The Central Elections Committee announced that counting of the votes cast in outer envelopes, also known as double-envelope ballots, began at 1:00 a.m., following the completion of the required intake, scanning, and verification procedures.
As part of the process, the inner ballot envelopes are removed from the outer envelopes and mixed together to ensure that voters' identities cannot be linked to their ballots, preserving the secrecy of the vote. The ballots are then transferred for counting at the counting facility in the Knesset parking lot.
Meanwhile, the committee reported that the processing of results from regular polling stations is continuing. As of 1:00 a.m., results had been received from 11,712 of the 12,018 regular polling stations, where 5,126,759 voters cast their ballots. The remaining polling stations are undergoing routine verification procedures.
